title: Diagonals Separated Morphisms and Valuative Uniqueness

items.title: Immersion of schemes
items.statement: An immersion is a morphism factoring as a closed immersion into an open subscheme of its target; its image carries the induced locally closed subscheme structure.
items.strategy: Use the standard open-neighborhood definition; factorization is not part of the intrinsic morphism and changes of ambient open preserve the induced local structure.

items.title: Separated morphism of schemes
items.statement: A morphism f:X→S is separated exactly when Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X is a closed immersion. Quasi-separated means that this diagonal is quasi-compact; neither property is a condition on the point-set topology of X alone.
items.strategy: Use the fibre-product diagonal and the existing closed-immersion and quasi-compact conventions.

items.title: Closed immersions are local on the target
items.statement: Let i:Z→X be a morphism of schemes and let X=∪_j V_j be an open cover. Then i is a closed immersion if and only if the restriction i^{-1}(V_j)→V_j is a closed immersion for every j.
items.strategy: Restrict the homeomorphism-onto-closed-image and the stalkwise surjectivity of the structure map to each open; conversely glue injectivity, closedness of the image and stalkwise surjectivity from an open cover of the target.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma 26.4.2 (tag 01HL), printed p.5

items.title: Separated S-scheme
items.statement: An S-scheme X is separated over S when its structure morphism X→S is separated. Absolutely separated means separated over Spec Z. Relative and absolute conventions must name their base.
items.strategy: Define both relative and absolute language using the separated-morphism definition. Any equivalence for an affine base is a separate theorem, not part of this definition.

items.title: Every scheme diagonal is an immersion
items.statement: For every morphism of schemes X→S, Δ_{X/S} is an immersion. It identifies X with a locally closed subscheme of X×_S X; a point of the product lies in its image precisely when the two projections are the same point with the same induced residue-field map.
items.strategy: Cover the diagonal image by U×_V U for affine U⊂X mapping into affine V⊂S. Each restricted diagonal is Spec of multiplication B⊗_A B→B, hence closed in this open neighborhood. Distinguish scheme-valued equality from mere equality of underlying points.

items.title: Affine morphisms are separated
items.statement: Every affine morphism f:X→S is separated, without Noetherian, reducedness or finite-type hypotheses.
items.strategy: Check separatedness on an affine open cover of S: for A→B the diagonal has surjective multiplication map B⊗_A B→B. Glue the closed-immersion condition on the target.

items.title: Affine schemes and affine morphisms are separated
items.statement: Any morphism Spec B→Spec A is separated; every affine scheme is absolutely separated over Spec Z. More generally an affine morphism to any scheme is separated.
items.strategy: Apply affine-morphism separatedness, including A=Z and the zero-ring/empty case. Do not infer affineness from separatedness.

items.title: Separatedness survives base change
items.statement: For any f:X→S separated and S′→S, the base change X×_S S′→S′ is separated.
items.strategy: Use the Cartesian diagonal identification and stability of closed immersions under arbitrary base change.

items.title: Separated morphisms compose
items.statement: If X→Y and Y→S are separated, then X→S is separated.
items.strategy: Factor Δ_{X/S} as Δ_{X/Y} followed by X×_Y X→X×_S X; identify the latter as a pullback of Δ_{Y/S}, then compose two closed immersions.

items.title: Separatedness is local on the base
items.statement: For an open cover S=∪S_i, f:X→S is separated iff each restriction X×_S S_i→S_i is separated.
items.strategy: The open subsets X_i×_{S_i}X_i cover X×_S X. A morphism is a closed immersion iff it is so after restriction to an open cover of its target; apply to the diagonal.

items.title: Monomorphisms and diagonals
items.statement: A scheme morphism j:X→Y is a monomorphism iff Δ_{X/Y}:X→X×_Y X is an isomorphism; every monomorphism is separated.
items.strategy: Yoneda: two test maps to X over Y coincide exactly when the diagonal supplies an inverse to the product projection. An isomorphism is a closed immersion.

items.title: Closed graphs over separated targets
items.statement: If Y→S is separated, the graph Γ_g:X→X×_S Y of every S-morphism g:X→Y is a closed immersion; no separatedness of X/S is required.
items.strategy: Use the published Cartesian graph square as a base change of Δ_{Y/S}.

items.title: Equalizers into separated schemes are closed
items.statement: For S-morphisms a,b:X⇉Y with Y→S separated, their equalizer E=X×_{(a,b),Y×_S Y,Δ_{Y/S}}Y exists as a closed subscheme of X and represents agreement on every test scheme, including nonreduced ones.
items.strategy: Form (a,b), pull back the closed diagonal, and verify the fibre-product universal property. Do not substitute the set of equal points for the equalizer scheme.

items.title: Agreement on a schematically dense open
items.statement: Assume AC. If Y/S is separated and U⊂X is schematically dense (O_X→j_*O_U injective), two S-morphisms X⇉Y equal on U are equal on X. In particular this holds when X is reduced and U is a topologically dense open subscheme.
items.strategy: The equalizer ideal vanishes on U; schematic density forces it to vanish on X. For reduced X and dense U a nonzero section s would give a nonempty basic open D(s) disjoint from U, using [F5] to produce a prime of the nonzero localization A_s.

items.title: Quasi-separatedness and the diagonal
items.statement: A scheme morphism is quasi-separated iff its diagonal is quasi-compact; equivalently, over affine opens U,V⊂X mapping into one affine open of S, each U∩V is quasi-compact, hence a finite union of affine opens.
items.strategy: The published definition of quasi-separatedness uses quasi-compact affine intersections. For affine U,V over one affine W⊂S, the target product U×_W V is affine and Δ^{-1}(U×_W V)=U∩V. Such products form an affine open cover of X×_S X; quasi-compactness of a morphism is local on this target cover, so the intersection condition is equivalent to quasi-compactness of Δ.

items.title: Valuative uniqueness diagram
items.statement: For a valuation ring R with fraction field K, a valuative diagram for f:X→S consists of Spec K→X above Spec R→S. Uniqueness means at most one compatible Spec R→X; existence means at least one. The criterion ranges over all such R,K, base maps and field extensions.
items.strategy: State both quantifiers separately. The generic map need not extend; uniqueness is then vacuous for that diagram.

items.title: Separatedness implies valuative uniqueness
items.statement: For any separated morphism f:X→S, any valuation ring R with fraction field K, and any compatible Spec K→X over Spec R→S, there is at most one extension Spec R→X. No quasi-separatedness, finite type or Choice hypothesis is required.
items.strategy: Pull back Δ_{X/S} along a pair of proposed lifts. Its equalizer is closed in integral Spec R and contains the generic point; a closed subscheme of Spec R containing the generic point is all of Spec R because R is a domain.

items.title: A quasi-compact immersion with nonclosed image has a boundary specialization
items.statement: Assume AC. If a quasi-compact immersion j:Z→T has nonclosed image, some point η in j(Z) specializes to a point t in its closure outside j(Z).
items.strategy: Choose an affine neighborhood of t and finitely many affine-local pieces of the inverse image, each a closed subscheme of a distinguished open D(f) in that neighborhood. A finite union of closures contains t, so one piece does. In A_p/I, with p=t, f is not nilpotent; the proper ideal argument yields q⊂p containing I and avoiding f. This q is the required η. AC supplies the prime/maximal ideal via Zorn; finite cover comes from quasi-compactness.

items.title: A local domain has a dominating valuation overring
items.statement: Assume AC. If A⊂K is a local subring of a field K, there is a valuation ring V⊂K with fraction field K whose local inclusion dominates A.
items.strategy: Order local subrings of K dominating A by domination. Unions of chains are local, so Zorn gives a maximal one V. If Frac(V)≠K, adjoin a transcendental element and localize, or adjoin an integral multiple of an algebraic element and use lying over, contradicting maximality. With Frac(V)=K, for x∈K× with x∉V no prime of V[x] can lie over m_V, so m_V V[x]=V[x] by the maximal-ideal theorem; a finite relation 1=Σa_i x^i with a_i∈m_V makes x^{-1} integral over V, so x^{-1}∈V. Thus V satisfies the inversion characterization. AC is used in Zorn, in lying over and in the maximal-ideal step producing a prime over m_V.

items.title: An immersion with closed image is a closed immersion
items.statement: Let i:Z→X be an immersion of schemes. If the image i(Z) is closed in X, then i is a closed immersion.
items.strategy: Factor the immersion as a closed immersion into an open subscheme; if the image is closed, check the two closed-immersion clauses on stalks, where the open immersion contributes an isomorphism.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma 26.10.4, printed p.18

items.title: Valuative uniqueness detects separatedness
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a quasi-separated morphism of schemes f:X→S, f is separated iff every valuative diagram with arbitrary valuation ring R and fraction field K has at most one lift. This does not assert existence; a finite-type morphism is included only when it is quasi-separated.
items.strategy: The forward implication is the preceding choice-free equalizer lemma. Conversely, Δ is a quasi-compact immersion. If its image were not closed, the boundary-specialization lemma gives η in the diagonal specializing to t outside it. Give W=closure{η} its reduced integral scheme structure; A=O_{W,t} is a local domain contained in κ(η). The valuation-overring lemma gives V⊂κ(η) dominating A. The map Spec V→W→X×_S X sends the generic point to η and the closed point to t. Its projections are two V-maps to X agreeing on Frac V because η lies in Δ, but differing at t, contradicting uniqueness. Thus the diagonal image is closed; an immersion with closed image is a closed immersion. AC is used exactly in the boundary prime and valuation-overring constructions. Quantify over all valuation rings, not just DVRs.

items.title: Immersions are monomorphisms locally of finite type
items.statement: Every immersion of schemes is a monomorphism and is locally of finite type; it is therefore separated. Finite presentation is not claimed for a closed immersion with a non-finitely-generated ideal.
items.strategy: Open immersions are locally isomorphisms onto open subschemes, so on a suitable affine chart the corresponding ring map is an identity; closed immersions restrict to quotients A→A/I generated by one element. Compose the two and apply the diagonal characterization of monomorphisms.

items.title: Open and closed immersions are separated
items.statement: Every open or closed immersion is separated, as is every locally closed immersion.
items.strategy: Each is a monomorphism; the diagonal is an isomorphism and hence a closed immersion.

items.title: Affine-overlap criterion for separatedness
items.statement: For f:X→S, choose an affine cover S=∪W_i and affine covers of each f^{-1}W_i. Then f is separated iff, for every pair U=Spec B,V=Spec C in a common chosen cover over W_i=Spec A, the intersection U∩V is affine and B⊗_A C→Γ(U∩V,O_X) is surjective. The same condition may be checked for all affine pairs lying over one affine base open.
items.strategy: The pullback of Δ to U×_W V is U∩V→Spec(B⊗_A C). It is a closed immersion exactly when the intersection is affine and the coordinate map is surjective. These products cover X×_S X; empty overlaps use the zero ring. Affine intersection alone is insufficient (doubled origin).

items.title: The affine line with doubled origin is not separated
items.statement: Let D be two copies of A¹_k glued along G_m over a field k. Then D→Spec k is quasi-separated but not separated; its two origins give distinct lifts of the same map Spec k(t)→D from Spec k[t]_(t).
items.strategy: The cross-chart overlap is Spec k[t,t^{-1}], and k[x]⊗_k k[y]→k[t,t^{-1}] is not surjective because t^{-1} is absent from the polynomial image. The quasi-compact overlap gives quasi-separatedness. The two DVR lifts are a second direct witness, independent of the converse valuative theorem.

items.title: Relative projective space from standard charts
items.statement: For n≥0, construct P^n_Z by gluing n+1 copies of Spec Z[t_0,…,t_n]/(t_i−1) along D(t_j) using t_ℓ/t_i=(t_ℓ/t_j)/(t_i/t_j); define P^n_S=S×_{Spec Z}P^n_Z. The standard charts are affine over S and commute with base change; they are affine schemes when S is affine, including the cases S=∅ and n=0.
items.strategy: Check reciprocal coordinate transition and triple cocycle, apply affine-scheme gluing, then base-change the charts. This supplies an actual relative scheme; the earlier classical projective-point definition alone is inadequate over arbitrary S.

items.title: The relative projective-space diagonal is closed
items.statement: For every scheme S and n≥0, Δ_{P^n_S/S} is a closed immersion. On U_i×_S U_j over Spec A, the mixed-chart kernel is generated by (x_j/x_i)(y_i/y_j)−1 and (y_m/y_j)−(x_m/x_i)(y_i/y_j) for m≠i,j; on a same-chart product it is generated by the coordinate differences. These are dehomogenized 2×2 minors x_a y_b−x_b y_a. Thus P^n_S→S is separated.
items.strategy: Reduce to affine S=Spec A. For i≠j, the overlap U_i∩U_j=D(x_j/x_i) is affine; under the chart coordinate map y_i/y_j goes to (x_j/x_i)^{-1} and y_m/y_j goes to (x_m/x_i)(x_j/x_i)^{-1}. Quotienting by the displayed polynomial kernel identifies the source with the overlap ring; apply the affine-overlap criterion and base locality.

items.title: Separated is not Zariski Hausdorff
items.statement: A scheme is separated by a closed scheme-theoretic diagonal. The underlying topological space of X×_S X generally differs from the topological product |X|×|X|, so separated schemes such as A¹_k have non-Hausdorff Zariski point spaces.
items.strategy: Use the generic point of Spec k[t] as a specialization witness and the affine diagonal as the separatedness witness.

items.title: The valuative criterion quantifies over all valuation rings
items.statement: Under AC, the quasi-separated valuative uniqueness criterion quantifies over arbitrary valuation rings and fraction fields. DVR-only uniqueness needs additional hypotheses such as a finite-type morphism between locally Noetherian schemes; no such reduction is implicit here.
items.strategy: Distinguish Stacks §26.22.2 from Vakil §13.7.1. The B-page non-Noetherian glued valuation example demonstrates a genuine failure of unrestricted DVR reduction.

title: Diagonals Separated Morphisms and Valuative Uniqueness — Examples

items.title: The diagonal of the affine line
items.statement: For A¹_S over affine S=Spec A, the diagonal in Spec A[x,y] has ideal (x−y); the formula glues over arbitrary S.
items.strategy: Use multiplication A[x]⊗_A A[x]→A[x], whose kernel is (x−y).

items.title: The projective-line diagonal from the bihomogeneous equation
items.statement: In P¹_S×_S P¹_S, the diagonal is the closed subscheme cut out by x_0y_1−x_1y_0=0, interpreted on every standard chart.
items.strategy: Check the four chart pairs: the displayed equation becomes the equality of affine ratios, and each localized coordinate map is surjective.

items.title: The doubled-origin diagonal is not closed
items.statement: For the doubled-origin line D over k, Δ_{D/k}(D) is not closed in D×_kD: the cross-chart generic diagonal specializes to the pair of distinct origins.
items.strategy: In the cross chart Spec k[x,y], the diagonal over G_m is {(t,t):t≠0}; its closure is V(x−y), containing (0_1,0_2), which is absent from Δ.

items.title: Two DVR lifts of one diagram over the doubled-origin line
items.statement: The map Spec k(t)→D landing in the shared G_m and the structure map Spec k[t]_(t)→Spec k admit two distinct compatible lifts to D, one with each origin as special point.
items.strategy: Both chart inclusions extend the same generic coordinate t; distinguish their closed-point images.

items.title: The graph of a polynomial map as a closed subscheme
items.statement: For a polynomial map g:A^m_k→A^n_k with coordinate polynomials g_j, Γ_g⊂A^m_k×_kA^n_k is cut out by y_j−g_j(x), and its projection to A^m_k is an isomorphism.
items.strategy: The quotient of k[x_1,…,x_m,y_1,…,y_n] by these equations is k[x_1,…,x_m]. Identify this with the abstract closed graph.

items.title: A separated scheme whose point space is not Hausdorff
items.statement: For every field k, A¹_k is separated over k, but its Zariski space is not Hausdorff: its generic point lies in every nonempty open set and cannot be separated from the closed origin.
items.strategy: Affine separatedness comes from the diagonal; topology uses irreducibility of Spec k[t] and the specialization of (0) to (t).

items.title: An open immersion has valuative uniqueness but not existence
items.statement: For j:D(t)↪Spec k[t], every valuation-ring diagram has at most one lift, but Spec k[t]_(t)→Spec k[t] with its generic point in D(t) has no lift to D(t).
items.strategy: An open immersion is a monomorphism, giving uniqueness. A lift of the displayed DVR map would send the closed point into D(t), contrary to t lying in its maximal ideal.

items.title: DVR uniqueness need not detect nonseparatedness
items.statement: Let V=∪_{n≥1} k[t^{1/n}]_(t^{1/n}) inside K=∪_{n≥1}k(t^{1/n}) (transition indices by divisibility), and let X be two copies of Spec V glued along Spec K. Then X→Spec V is quasi-separated and not separated, but every valuative diagram using a DVR has at most one lift. The V-valuative diagram has two lifts.
items.strategy: V has rank-one value group Q and exactly two primes (0,m); Spec K is quasi-compact. Cross-chart overlap map V⊗_V V→K is not surjective, so X/V is nonseparated. A DVR diagram giving two lifts would have generic image in Spec K and closed image in the two distinct closed points, forcing a local injective V→DVR. But the image of t would have positive integer valuation divisible by every n via t^{1/n}, impossible. A V-valuative diagram uses the two chart inclusions. Field valuation rings are allowed in the full criterion but are not DVRs under the published convention; their sole point is fixed by the specified generic map.

title: Kahler Differentials Conormal Sequences and Infinitesimal Lifting

items.title: Derivation of an algebra
items.statement: For a ring map A→B and B-module M, an A-derivation D:B→M is additive, kills the image of A, and satisfies D(bb′)=bD(b′)+b′D(b). The set Der_A(B,M) is a B-module.
items.strategy: State the Leibniz and A-constant laws; D is A-linear, not generally B-linear. No finiteness is assumed.

items.title: Universal Kähler differential module
items.statement: For A→B, a Kähler differential module is a pair (Ω_{B/A},d:B→Ω_{B/A}) representing the functor M↦Der_A(B,M) on B-modules. Such a pair, if it exists, is unique up to unique compatible isomorphism.
items.strategy: Specify the natural bijection Hom_B(Ω,M)≅Der_A(B,M) and its functoriality in M; existence is established next.

items.title: Existence and generators of Kähler differentials
items.statement: For every A→B, Ω_{B/A} exists as the free B-module on symbols db, b∈B, modulo d(b+b′)−db−db′, d(bb′)−bdb′−b′db, and da for a∈A. The class b↦db is universal.
items.strategy: Construct the free module with finite-support formal sums; check the relations make d a derivation. A derivation to M kills precisely those relators, so its assignment on symbols descends uniquely. Compare with the earlier algebraic-differentials interface and retain the full generality.

items.title: Derivations are maps out of Ω
items.statement: For every B-module M, composition with d gives a natural B-module isomorphism Hom_B(Ω_{B/A},M)≅Der_A(B,M).
items.strategy: Map a homomorphism to its composite with d, and invert by the generator assignment from the presentation. Verify compatibility with B-module maps M→N.

items.title: Polynomial differentials are free
items.statement: For P=A[x_1,…,x_n], n≥0, Ω_{P/A} is free on dx_1,…,dx_n; at n=0 the module is zero. A derivation is uniquely determined by arbitrary images of the variables.
items.strategy: Use the polynomial universal property to extend any n-tuple in M to a derivation; the derivations functor is Hom_P(P^n,M). Invoke representability and compare universal elements.

items.title: Conormal exact sequence for an algebra quotient
items.statement: For A→P and ideal I⊂P, B=P/I, the canonical sequence I/I²→B⊗_PΩ_{P/A}→Ω_{B/A}→0 is exact, with [i]↦1⊗di. No injectivity of the first arrow is asserted.
items.strategy: Check d(I²)⊂IΩ. The quotient imposing di=0 for i∈I represents A-derivations of B, so equals Ω_{B/A}; these relations generate exactly the kernel.

items.title: Jacobian presentation of Ω
items.statement: If P=A[x_1,…,x_n] and I=(f_1,…,f_r), then Ω_{(P/I)/A} is the cokernel of B^r→B^n whose jth column is (∂f_j/∂x_i)_i. This is a presentation, not a smoothness criterion by itself.
items.strategy: Insert the polynomial free basis in the conormal sequence; [f_j] generate I/I² and d f_j=Σ_i(∂f_j/∂x_i)dx_i.

items.title: Transitivity sequence for differential modules
items.statement: For A→B→C there is a natural right-exact sequence C⊗_BΩ_{B/A}→Ω_{C/A}→Ω_{C/B}→0. No left injectivity is claimed.
items.strategy: The right map imposes db=0 for b∈B, so is surjective and has kernel the C-span of those db; this is the image of the first map. Check the maps via the universal derivation.

items.title: Kähler differentials commute with localization
items.statement: For A→B, a multiplicative U⊂B, and V⊂A mapping into U, the canonical map U^{-1}Ω_{B/A}→Ω_{U^{-1}B/V^{-1}A} is an isomorphism. In particular V={1} is allowed.
items.strategy: Extend a derivation uniquely by D(b/u)=u^{-1}D(b)−bu^{-2}D(u); restrictions and extensions are inverse. Use the universal property for arbitrary localized modules.

items.title: Kähler differentials commute with scalar base change
items.statement: For A→B and A→A′, set B′=B⊗_A A′. Then the canonical B′-linear map Ω_{B/A}⊗_B B′→Ω_{B′/A′} is an isomorphism. It does not assert that Ω is unchanged under an arbitrary map B→C.
items.strategy: An A′-derivation B′→M restricts to an A-derivation B→M, and the latter extends by D(b⊗a′)=a′D(b); the two constructions are inverse. Represent both functors.

items.title: Sheaf of relative Kähler differentials
items.statement: For f:X→S, form the presheaf W↦Ω_{O_X(W)/(f^{-1}O_S)(W)} and sheafify it to obtain Ω_{X/S} with its universal S-derivation d:O_X→Ω_{X/S}. The affine-chart compatibility is proved separately.
items.strategy: Define the restriction maps by the algebraic universal property; sheafify the module presheaf and its compatible derivations. Use the subsequent universal-property and affine-compatibility items to justify local descriptions.

items.title: Universal property of relative differential sheaves
items.statement: For any O_X-module F, precomposition with d yields a natural bijection Hom_{O_X}(Ω_{X/S},F)≅Der_S(O_X,F), where derivations are local sheaf maps satisfying Leibniz and killing f^{-1}O_S.
items.strategy: On each affine chart, the algebraic universal property identifies morphisms and derivations; restriction is compatible by localization, so the local maps glue uniquely. No quasi-coherence assumption on F is needed.

items.title: The sheaf attached to a module on an affine scheme
items.statement: For a commutative ring B, a B-module M and X=Spec B, the sheafification of U↦M⊗_B O_X(U) represents the functor F↦Hom_B(M,F(X)): Hom_{O_X}(M~,F)≅Hom_B(M,F(X)), naturally in M and F; M↦M~ is a functor, right exact, with B~≅O_X and Γ(X,B~)=B. No finiteness on M or B.
items.strategy: Construct M~ as the sheafification of the presheaf M⊗_B O_X(U); the universal property of sheafification reduces morphisms to compatible families over basic opens, and the tensor universal property converts the B-linearity of g:M→F(X) into O_X(U)-linearity over each U; right exactness from sheafification and tensor right exactness; Γ(X,B~)=B via the identification at the bottom.

references.title: Stacks Modules, Definition 17.10.1 (tag 01BE), Lemma 17.10.5 (tag 01BH) and Definition 17.10.6 (tag 01BI)

items.title: Affine charts recover the algebraic module of differentials
items.statement: If X=Spec B→S=Spec A, then Ω_{X/S}≅\widetilde{Ω_{B/A}} with d on global sections the algebraic universal derivation; restriction to D(g) corresponds to localization at g.
items.strategy: Compare the glued affine construction with the associated module on standard opens and use uniqueness of the universal object.

items.title: Conormal sequence for a closed immersion
items.statement: For a closed immersion i:X↪Y over S with ideal sheaf I, there is an exact sequence I/I²→i^*Ω_{Y/S}→Ω_{X/S}→0 of O_X-modules. The left map is not generally injective.
items.strategy: Restrict to affine charts, apply the algebraic conormal sequence, then use stalkwise exactness and compatibility of pullback with tensor. Check that d(I²)⊂IΩ defines the first sheaf map independently of charts.

items.title: Transitivity sequence for schemes
items.statement: For X→^fY→S, there is a natural exact sequence f^*Ω_{Y/S}→Ω_{X/S}→Ω_{X/Y}→0; the first arrow need not be injective.
items.strategy: Check affine charts and sheafify the algebraic transitivity sequence; exactness is stalkwise. Identify the first map through the universal derivation.

items.title: Relative differentials commute with scheme base change
items.statement: For X→S and S′→S with projection g:X×_S S′→X, the canonical map g^*Ω_{X/S}→Ω_{X×_S S′/S′} is an isomorphism.
items.strategy: Reduce on affines to Ω_{B/A}⊗_B(B⊗_A A′)≅Ω_{(B⊗_A A′)/A′}; verify compatibility on overlaps and glue.

items.title: Relative cotangent and tangent spaces
items.statement: For x∈X over s∈S, the relative cotangent space is Ω_{X/S}⊗_{O_{X,x}}κ(x); its κ(x)-linear dual is the relative tangent space T_{X/S,x}. These fibres retain the chosen residue-field map κ(s)→κ(x).
items.strategy: Take the stalk followed by residue-field tensor; define dual over κ(x), not over κ(s) unless specified.

items.title: Cotangent space at a rational point
items.statement: Let X be a k-scheme and x∈X a k-rational point. With m_x⊂O_{X,x}, the map [a]↦da⊗1 induces a natural κ(x)=k-linear isomorphism m_x/m_x²≅Ω_{X/k}⊗κ(x). No analogous claim for arbitrary inseparable residue fields is made.
items.strategy: The conormal sequence for O_{X,x}→k gives surjectivity. Since k→O_{X,x}/m_x² splits the residue map, the square-zero quotient is k⊕m_x/m_x²; its projection onto the ideal is a k-derivation and supplies a left inverse to d. Or identify both duals with k-derivations, with the explicit split map avoiding finite-dimensional duality.

items.title: Tangent vectors as dual-number points
items.statement: For x∈X over S, S-morphisms Spec κ(x)[ε]/(ε²)→X whose reduction is the canonical κ(x)-point x are naturally the vectors Hom_{κ(x)}(Ω_{X/S}⊗κ(x),κ(x)). At a k-rational point this recovers the usual tangent space.
items.strategy: The map of local rings sends a↦a(x)+εD(a). Ring multiplicativity is exactly Leibniz; base compatibility means D kills S. Use the differential universal property, and check both directions and the fixed residue-field identification.

references.title: Stacks Morphisms §29.33; Stacks Properties of Schemes §28.16

items.title: Differential of an S-morphism
items.statement: For an S-morphism f:X→Y, universal derivations induce df:f^*Ω_{Y/S}→Ω_{X/S}. At x over y, its cotangent fibre has source (Ω_{Y/S,y}⊗κ(y))⊗_{κ(y)}κ(x); dualising over κ(x) gives a tangent map into the dual of that extended cotangent space. Identity and composition obey the chain rule.
items.strategy: Represent the S-derivation O_Y→f_*Ω_{X/S} and adjoint to f^*. At x tensor the source stalk with κ(x), explicitly extending the cotangent space at y along κ(y)→κ(x), then dualise. Check identity and chain rule on universal differentials; composition of pullbacks follows from associativity of the sheaf tensor products defining pullback.

items.title: Formally unramified morphism
items.statement: A morphism f:X→S is formally unramified when every commutative S-diagram T_0↪T with square-zero defining ideal and T_0→X has at most one compatible lift T→X. The condition is uniqueness only and imposes no finite-type hypothesis.
items.strategy: Quantify over all square-zero closed immersions of S-schemes, and include nonaffine tests.

references.title: Stacks Algebra §10.148.1 and Stacks More Morphisms §37.6

items.title: Formally smooth morphism
items.statement: A morphism f:X→S is formally smooth when each square-zero lifting problem T_0↪T over S has lifts Zariski locally on the test scheme T around every point of T_0. No uniqueness is required; the condition is local on the test source.
items.strategy: State the local existence quantifier for test thickenings precisely; distinguish it from global existence for affine tests and from a finite-presentation smooth morphism.

items.title: Formally étale morphism
items.statement: A morphism is formally étale when it is both formally smooth and formally unramified. Equivalently, every square-zero lifting problem has a unique lift locally on the test scheme, and those unique lifts glue.
items.strategy: Combine local existence with uniqueness on overlaps; the sheaf property for morphisms glues the local lifts. No finite-presentation condition enters.

items.title: The diagonal ideal modulo its square is Ω
items.statement: For A→B let J=ker(B⊗_A B→B), multiplication. The B-linear map Ω_{B/A}→J/J² given by db↦1⊗b−b⊗1 is an isomorphism. It is natural in A→B.
items.strategy: The displayed difference is an A-derivation modulo J². Conversely J is generated by 1⊗b−b⊗1; send such generators to db, and verify products of two differences vanish. Check both compositions on generators, including the sign convention.

items.title: Formal unramifiedness iff Ω vanishes
items.statement: For any scheme morphism f:X→S, f is formally unramified iff Ω_{X/S}=0; neither finite type nor separatedness is assumed.
items.strategy: If Ω=0, the difference of two lifts across a square-zero ideal is an S-derivation into that ideal and must vanish locally. Conversely, the two projections of the first-order diagonal thickening defined by J² agree on the closed diagonal; formal uniqueness forces their difference to vanish, so J/J²=0 on affine diagonal neighborhoods. Use the diagonal-ideal lemma and sheaf compatibility.

items.title: Unramified morphism
items.statement: A scheme morphism f:X→S is unramified when it is locally of finite type and formally unramified, equivalently when it is locally of finite type and Ω_{X/S}=0. Locally of finite presentation gives the stronger G-unramified convention.
items.strategy: Make the finite-type versus finite-presentation convention explicit and apply the formal-unramified differential criterion.

items.title: An unramified morphism has an open diagonal
items.statement: If f:X→S is unramified, Δ_{X/S} is an open immersion. Conversely, if f is locally of finite type and Δ_{X/S} is an open immersion, then f is unramified. No separatedness is needed.
items.strategy: Near a point of the diagonal work on affine A→B of finite type. The diagonal ideal J is generated by b_i⊗1−1⊗b_i for finite algebra generators. Ω=J/J²=0 makes J=J². Apply the determinant trick to the finite module J: some e∈J satisfies (1−e)J=0; then e²=e and J=e(B⊗_A B). Hence this closed diagonal is the complementary open-and-closed component. These neighborhoods cover the diagonal image, so the immersion is open. Conversely an open diagonal has zero conormal sheaf, hence Ω=0 by the diagonal-ideal identification; apply the finite-type definition.

items.title: A field has only the zero ideal and itself, hence is Noetherian
items.statement: A field K has exactly the ideals (0) and K; both are generated by one element, so every ideal of K is finitely generated and K is a Noetherian ring. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: An ideal containing a nonzero element contains its inverse times it, hence 1, hence is the unit ideal; the two remaining ideals are generated by 0 and 1, so the equivalent ideal-wise form of the Noetherian condition applies.

references.title: Stacks Project, Algebra, Section 10.31 (tag 00FM) and Lemma 10.31.3 (tag 00FO)

items.title: Finite-type field extensions with zero Ω
items.statement: Assume AC. If L/k is a finitely generated field extension and Ω_{L/k}=0, then L/k is finite separable. Conversely every finite separable extension has Ω=0.
items.strategy: Choose finite-type domain B⊂L with Frac B=L. Ω_{B/k} is finite, so after inverting one nonzero f it vanishes. Over an algebraic closure K of k, base change preserves Ω. Present C=B_f⊗K as a finite-type K-algebra. Each maximal ideal of C is K-rational by Nullstellensatz and has m/m²=0 by the rational cotangent theorem; Nakayama makes C_m a field. The Hilbert basis theorem makes C Noetherian. Every prime lies under a maximal ideal, hence equals it, so the finitely many minimal primes are precisely all the maximal ideals. All maximal localizations are fields, so C is reduced. The Chinese remainder theorem yields C≅∏C/m_i≅K^r. Faithful scalar extension then makes B_f finite-dimensional over k; as a domain it is a field equal to L. If L/k were inseparable, an inseparable minimal polynomial would create a nonzero nilpotent in L⊗_kK, contradicting reducedness. For the converse differentiate separable minimal polynomials (or a primitive element). AC is used to obtain K and in maximal-ideal/Nullstellensatz steps.

items.title: Unramified residue extensions are finite separable
items.statement: Assume AC. If f:X→S is locally of finite type at x and Ω_{X/S,x}=0, then κ(x)/κ(f(x)) is finite separable and m_{f(x)}O_{X,x}=m_x. This applies in particular to an unramified or locally finite type formally étale map at x; the later étale page proves the corresponding smooth/flat characterization.
items.strategy: Base-change to the fibre over s=f(x); Ω of the finite-type fibre vanishes at x. Its image in Ω_{κ(x)/κ(s)} is zero, so the finite-type field lemma gives finite separability. The separable-residue cotangent sequence on the fibre injects m_x/m_x² into Ω_fibre⊗κ(x)=0; Nakayama makes the fibre local ring a field, equivalent to m_sO_{X,x}=m_x. Track localization and the finite-type neighbourhood. AC is inherited from the finite-type field lemma and the published Nakayama theorem; the separable-residue supplier itself is choice-free.

items.title: Relative differential-rank condition
items.statement: For n≥0, f:X→S has differential rank n on an open U⊂X if Ω_{X/S}|_U is locally free of constant rank n. On a nonempty U this rank is unique; on the empty open every n satisfies the condition. Differential rank alone does not define smoothness.
items.strategy: Define only the locally free rank condition. On a standard presentation invert a c-by-c Jacobian minor and use the transposed relation map to exhibit the free rank n=N-c cokernel; do not infer smoothness from rank alone.

items.title: The conormal sequence is only right exact
items.statement: In I/I²→Ω_{P/A}⊗_P(P/I)→Ω_{(P/I)/A}→0, the left arrow can have a nonzero kernel. For P=k[x], I=(x²), the class [x³] is nonzero in I/I²=(x²)/(x⁴) but maps to d(x³)=3x²dx=0 in the quotient.
items.strategy: The explicit class works in every characteristic; distinguish this from a regular-immersion claim, where extra hypotheses can give injectivity.

items.title: Differential rank alone does not prove smoothness
items.statement: Vanishing or local freeness of Ω controls first-order infinitesimal behavior, but smoothness needs additional finite-presentation, flatness and geometric-fibre hypotheses. In characteristic p, Frobenius shows that zero differential and zero dual fibre maps are not an étaleness test.
items.strategy: Separate the relative differential module of a map from the induced map on absolute differentials; cite the flatness and fibre warnings without using later smooth results as prerequisites.

title: Kahler Differentials Conormal Sequences and Infinitesimal Lifting — Examples

items.title: Differentials of k[x,y]
items.statement: Ω_{k[x,y]/k}=k[x,y]dx⊕k[x,y]dy, and d(x^a y^b)=a x^{a−1}y^b dx+b x^a y^{b−1}dy for a,b≥0, with zero terms at exponent zero.
items.strategy: Use the free polynomial basis and Leibniz induction; coefficients are read in k, so characteristic may annul them.

items.title: Differentials of a plane hypersurface
items.statement: For B=k[x,y]/(f), Ω_{B/k}≅(B dx⊕B dy)/B(f_xdx+f_ydy), with no regularity assumption on f.
items.strategy: Apply the one-relation Jacobian presentation; note f=0 and characteristic-dependent derivatives.

items.title: Differentials of dual numbers in both characteristics
items.statement: For B=k[ε]/(ε²), Ω_{B/k}=B dε/(2ε dε). If char k=2 it is free of rank one over B; otherwise ε dε=0 and it is one-dimensional over k.
items.strategy: Differentiate ε² and compute the cyclic quotient without assuming 2 invertible.

items.title: Finite separable extensions have zero Omega
items.statement: For every finite separable field extension L/k, Ω_{L/k}=0.
items.strategy: Use a primitive element α with separable minimal polynomial P, differentiate P(α)=0 to get P′(α)dα=0 and invert P′(α); generated elements then have zero differential.

items.title: A purely inseparable field has nonzero Ω
items.statement: In characteristic p, choose a∈k\k^p and L=k(α), α^p=a. Then Ω_{L/k}=L·dα≠0, even though L/k is finite algebraic.
items.strategy: The polynomial X^p−a is irreducible under the hypothesis; its derivative is zero, so the quotient differential presentation has no relation on dα.

items.title: A conormal left map with nonzero kernel
items.statement: For k[x]→B=k[x]/(x²), the class [x³] in (x²)/(x⁴) is nonzero but maps to zero in Ω_{k[x]/k}⊗B, in every characteristic.
items.strategy: Use [x³]=x[x²] and d(x³)=3x²dx, which vanishes modulo x²; x³∉(x⁴).

items.title: Dual-number vectors in affine space
items.statement: For x=(a_1,…,a_n)∈A^n_k(k), every dual-number point reducing to x sends coordinate X_i to a_i+εv_i, with unique v_i∈k; these are exactly the tangent vectors k^n.
items.strategy: A k-algebra map is determined by images of variables; reduction fixes constants and ε²=0 imposes no further equations for affine space. Match v_i with the dual basis to dX_i.

items.title: A closed point immersion is unramified
items.statement: For a field k and its reduced origin Spec k↪A¹_k, Ω_{Spec k/A¹_k}=0 and the immersion is unramified although it is not open. More generally every closed immersion is unramified under the locally finite type convention.
items.strategy: The coordinate map k[t]→k is surjective, so every derivation relative to k[t] is zero. A quotient is finite type as an algebra with zero generators; apply the definition.

items.title: Zero Frobenius tangent map does not imply formal étaleness
items.statement: Over k=F_p, absolute Frobenius F:A¹_k→A¹_k has zero induced map dF:F^*Ω_{A¹/k}→Ω_{A¹/k}, yet its relative module Ω_{A¹/A¹,F} is nonzero, so F is not formally unramified and hence not formally étale.
items.strategy: On coordinates F^*(dt)↦d(t^p)=0. For the ring map k[u]→k[t], u↦t^p, the relative presentation has Ω_{k[t]/k[u]}=k[t]dt because du maps to p t^{p−1}dt=0. Apply the formal-unramified criterion and keep the two differential notions distinct.
